values.value: You enforced law, maintained order, and operated inside a legal and procedural framework where documentation and accountability follow every decision. Whether you patrolled a base, managed a detention population, or ran investigations, you built judgment around use-of-force protocols, evidence handling, and chain-of-command accountability. That combination of authority, discipline, and procedural rigor is exactly what civilian law enforcement, corrections, investigations, and security leadership roles are built around.

[{"title": "Police Officer or Deputy Sheriff", "description": "You respond to calls, enforce laws, and make judgment calls in unpredictable situations. The work is part patrol, part documentation, and part community contact. Departments across the country run veterans preference programs and credit military law enforcement experience toward hiring and promotion. Most require a state POST certification or academy completion after hire — some states give partial credit for military training."}, {"title": "Federal Law Enforcement Officer", "description": "Agencies including CBP, ATF, U.S. Marshals, Secret Service, and ICE hire for roles where military discipline, weapons proficiency, and security experience are directly relevant. Federal LE agencies set entry age limits, often 37, but preference eligible veterans have two potential paths past that: the maximum entry age can be waived under 5 USC 3307, and agencies can separately extend the cutoff by the full length of your active duty service. Neither applies automatically — you have to claim it and provide your DD-214. If the age ceiling has you dismissing options, check your eligibility before you self-screen out."}, {"title": "Criminal Investigator", "description": "Federal criminal investigator positions — GS-1811 series — are staffed by agencies including the FBI, DEA, IRS Criminal Investigation, HSI, and U.S. Marshals. The work involves surveillance, interviews, evidence collection, and case documentation. Military intelligence, law enforcement, and investigative backgrounds are competitive. These positions carry law enforcement officer retirement and special pay."}, {"title": "Security Manager or Director", "description": "Corporate, healthcare, higher education, and government facilities hire security professionals to manage physical security programs, supervise teams, and build response plans for threats ranging from access control failures to active threats. Military police, master at arms, and security forces backgrounds translate directly. The ASIS Certified Protection Professional credential is the recognized industry benchmark for senior roles and is experience-based rather than requiring a formal degree."}, {"title": "Corrections Officer or Detention Officer", "description": "Federal and state corrections agencies hire veterans at competitive rates. Federal positions through the Bureau of Prisons are GS-series roles with law enforcement retirement benefits. State facilities vary by state civil service rules, most of which give veterans preference in scoring. The environment is structured, procedure-driven, and rewards the kind of composure and situational awareness you built in a military law enforcement or security role."}]
